item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.7
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 7

The app now comes in 24 languages. Choose one in Settings, General, Language; it sets the app's words and the language Tailwing expects to hear and writes notes in. The app asks you to restart for it to take effect. Separately, transcription covers all 25 languages Tailwing's speech model supports, Finnish included, so a meeting in Russian is still transcribed even though the app itself isn't in Russian.

Live translated subtitles. When a meeting is in a language other than yours, Tailwing asks once whether to translate it, with Always translate for that language. Subtitles appear at the bottom of the meeting window, and translation runs on this Mac.

You can also hear the translation spoken aloud in your own language, beside the subtitles. It's off by default; turn it on in Settings, Translation, with its own volume and speed. It needs a macOS voice for your language, and macOS has none yet for Estonian, Latvian or Maltese, so those stay subtitles only. Settings says where to download a better voice.

Private mode has its own group in Settings, Privacy, with three switches: Private mode, Hide everyone's names (the people in the meeting too, not only outsiders) and Private by default. Each says what it changes and what it costs: a meeting waits if names can't be removed. The meeting list now shows which meetings are private. Names are removed before text leaves this Mac, for every kind of send, including task notes and owners.

Write-ups use names rather than email addresses, check each owner against the people in the meeting, say a repeated point once and leave out filler and empty sections.

Settings tabs open without the pause, and there's a gear at the right end of the main window's toolbar, in every look. The Classic look follows the proportions of a 1990s desktop more closely.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.6
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 6

iCloud sync to Tailwing for iPhone works. A Mac that turned sync on in RC 5 sent nothing; it now sends the key, then meetings and notes, then audio a few parts at a time, so your meetings arrive first.

A meeting on an account that's in macOS Calendar and also signed in to Tailwing directly shows once. Copies from two different accounts are never joined.

Live coaching now all sits in the island by the camera. The island, the meeting banner, the dictation pill and the coaching cue say what they are when they appear, then shrink, and each can be dragged anywhere. Double-click an edge or choose Put Back to return one.

Dictation: the pill has a Copy button, a dictation that couldn't be typed stays on screen with its text, and Paste Last Dictation (Control-Command-V) types the last one again. In Mail, Outlook, and Gmail or Outlook on the web, dictated text is laid out as an email. Transcripts keep the spaces before numbers and rare words, and your own names are spelled right.

Audio is no longer kept by default: a new meeting's audio is deleted once its transcript and write-up are made. Audio from earlier meetings stays. Choose how long to keep audio in Settings, Privacy.

People are linked to an email address. Names without one stay as speaker labels in their meeting, and a voice that introduces itself is named.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.5
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 5

iCloud sync, for Tailwing for iPhone. Turn it on in Settings, Privacy. Meetings, notes, write-ups, transcripts and people sync through your own iCloud, encrypted. Audio syncs only if you choose. A private meeting never leaves this Mac.

Dictation is more reliable. It starts even while Tailwing is writing up or transcribing, a held key never stops mid-sentence, and every new sentence gets its space after the full stop, including where your text lands.

Long meetings now write up. They're written in parts, with progress shown, and a model that says a request is too long is asked again in smaller parts. Live coaching waits until notes are running. Its island sits flush against the top of the screen, says what it is, stays above other windows and keeps its text inside its frame. Right-click a folder or a person in the sidebar to rename them.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.4
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 4

Notes and write-ups are typeset for reading. Lines are a comfortable length, with spacing set for each look, bullets that hang in the margin, curly quotes and proper dashes, and figures that line up. Names with accents, such as Michał or Ștefan, now set in one typeface. Terminal stays dense and functional.

A meeting that appears on two of your calendars, or that a calendar tool copied from one to another, now shows as one meeting. Invites from other people are never merged into your own meetings, and a merge never changes a meeting's join link.

You can choose where alerts appear: automatically, under the Tailwing icon in the menu bar, at the top right or at the top left. Settings opens in its own window instead of as a tab, and the template choices explain what each one is for.
